subject: [PATCH 0/5] iomap: remaining patches for iomap_iter_next conversion

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Reviewed patches 1 and 2, finding the conversion to iomap_iter_next() model satisfactory. Suggested adding new creative iomap uses to relevant lists in patch 2.
reviews.raw_body:
On Tue, Oct 27, 2026 at 02:53:22PM -0700, Joanne Koong wrote:
> Convert nilfs2 iomap_ops to the new ->iomap_next() callback. The callback
> is generated with the DEFINE_IOMAP_ITER_NEXT() macro, which wraps the
> iomap_iter_next() helper to finish the previous mapping if needed and
> produce the next one. No functional changes are intended.

Looks good:

Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Found patch 2 satisfactory, but suggested adding new creative iomap uses to relevant lists.
reviews.raw_body:
Hmm, it would have been nice to CC adding a new creative iomap use
to the relevants lists..

Anyway, the conversion looks good:

Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>

2026-10-28.patch_summary: This patch series converts various filesystems to use the iomap_iter_next() model, which is a more efficient and flexible way of handling I/O operations. The patches are rebased on top of current mainline and require two new preparatory patches for trivial ->iomap_next() conversions. The conversion affects several filesystems, including nilfs2, fuse, ext4, exfat, and others.

reviews.author: Ryusuke Konishi
reviews.summary: Found the changes in patch 1 satisfactory, including the finalizing conversion in patch 4. Provided an Acked-by tag for patch 1.
reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, Oct 28, 2026 at 6:58 AM Joanne Koong wrote:
>
> Convert nilfs2 iomap_ops to the new ->iomap_next() callback. The callback
> is generated with the DEFINE_IOMAP_ITER_NEXT() macro, which wraps the
> iomap_iter_next() helper to finish the previous mapping if needed and
> produce the next one. No functional changes are intended.
>
> Signed-off-by: Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com>
> ---

Hi Joanne,

Thanks for picking up the newly merged NILFS2 iomap code and handling
the additional conversion to complete this series.

While this patch is an intermediate step, the changes look good to me,
including the finalizing conversion in patch 4/5.

Acked-by: Ryusuke Konishi <konishi.ryusuke@gmail.com>

Thanks,
Ryusuke Konishi

>  fs/nilfs2/iomap.c | 4 +++-
>  1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
>
> diff --git a/fs/nilfs2/iomap.c b/fs/nilfs2/iomap.c
> index e130ed63abd9..359786c97f2b 100644
> --- a/fs/nilfs2/iomap.c
> +++ b/fs/nilfs2/iomap.c
> @@ -67,6 +67,8 @@ static int nilfs_iomap_begin(struct inode *inode, loff_t offset,
>         return 0;
>  }
>
> +static DEFINE_IOMAP_ITER_NEXT(nilfs_iomap_next, nilfs_iomap_begin);
> +
>  const struct iomap_ops nilfs_iomap_ops = {
> -       .iomap_begin = nilfs_iomap_begin,
> +       .iomap_next = nilfs_iomap_next,
>  };
> --
> 2.52.0
>

reviews.author: Joanne Koong
reviews.summary: Provided an update on the patch series, stating that it still applies cleanly with no conflicts after rebasing on top of Linus's latest tree.
reviews.raw_body:
On Tue, Oct 27, 2026 at 2:58 PM Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> These patches are being sent out now in case anyone wants to look at the
> preparatory patches or patch 4. This series applies cleanly to both current
> mainline and next-20261027. If anything conflicts by the time you pick it up
> at the end of the merge window, I'll rebase and resend.
>

I pulled in Linus's latest tree (commit abf8c33470f7) and the series
still applies cleanly with no conflicts. It also applies cleanly on
top of next-20261030, which includes the remaining btrfs, ntfs, exfat,
ext2, and gfs2 changes that haven't been merged yet. There shouldn't
be any conflicts between this series and anything else going in this
window.

Thanks,
Joanne
